$comment: The lights the game has, named by hand. One list for the whole game, not one per level.
I.G.I. declares no lights at all: every lamp is geometry with a texture, and the light it appears
to cast was painted into a lightmap. LampDetector infers the rest from the shape of the geometry
and the pages it is skinned with, and it is an inference -- it misses fittings and it occasionally
lights furniture. This file is where somebody who has LOOKED says what is actually a lamp, and it
wins over anything inferred.
WHY IT IS NOT PER-MISSION. A model is a global asset: 226_01_1 is the same ceiling fitting in all
fourteen levels, and it binds the same textures in every one of them -- checked, for every model
the game names a light, across all fourteen. Nothing about a lamp changes between missions, so
keying this by mission only meant re-stating the same answer up to fourteen times and forgetting
it thirteen.
Additive, not exclusive. Naming a model here makes it a lamp; it does not stop the detector
finding others -- a fitting modelled INTO a building shell has no model of its own to name, and is
still found by shape. Use "lamp": false to say a model the detector picked is NOT one.
model     the instance name, as the F12 target readout prints it (OBJECT <model> ...).
textures  which of that model's sub-meshes emit, by the texture they draw with. A model is not
all lamp: a fitting is a dark housing around bright glass, a vending machine is a
cabinet with one lit panel, and a monitor is a desk with a screen on it. Omit to let
the brightest sub-mesh of the model be chosen.
radiance  how much light it appears to give off. 3 is an ordinary fitting; a floodlight is more,
and a lit advert or a screen is much less -- those are lit panels, not light sources.
The strength each texture is multiplied by is this over how bright the texture is, so
two fittings painted differently still arrive at the same brightness.
lamp      false to strike out a detection rather than add one.
note      what it is, for whoever reads this next.
title     which game the entry is about: "igi1" (the default) or "igi2".
TITLE MATTERS because the two games number their models out of the same range and DO
collide. I.G.I. 2 places models called 207_01_1 and 208_01_1, both hand-named lamps below --
of Project I.G.I.'s, not of its own. An unmarked entry is Project I.G.I.'s, which is what every
entry written before there was a second game is. The sequel has none here yet: its lamps are
detected rather than named, and naming one means looking at it first.
One catalogued fitting is deliberately absent: 303_04_1 (FLOODLIGHT), in ten of the levels. Its
three pages are a metal body it shares with the floodlight masts (302_02_1, mean 0.46) and two
near-black alpha sheets (0.04 and 0.03); it carries no bright page at all, so which part of it is
supposed to burn cannot be read off the art. It has never been lit and is left alone rather than
guessed at.

lamps.note: GARAGE_INTERIOR - the ceiling strip modelled into the garage shell
SODA_MACHINE - lit advert panel, not a lamp
FILINGCABINET - an office cabinet skinned with the ceiling lamp's own page (206_04_1), which is the one thing shaped and skinned like a fitting that is not one
